About the Team 
 DoorDash's mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about – helping grow business and the communities that support those businesses.
 About the Role 
 We’re looking for a business-savvy operator with a strong bias toward action to lead DoorDash Canada’s expansion and marketplace performance. As the national expansion lead, you’ll blend strategic thinking with operational excellence to identify growth opportunities, build strong internal partnerships, and improve customer and merchant experiences across the country.
 This role requires a proactive self-starter who thrives at the intersection of data, process management, and execution. Whether analyzing performance metrics for a new launch or engaging with cross-functional partners, you’ll uncover ways to improve market performance. Expansion is core to DoorDash Canada's growth, and we need someone who can apply best practices and right-size them for local geographies to ensure we are building a lasting product for our customers.
 We’re seeking someone who’s data-driven, a hands-on operator, relationship-oriented, and eager to make a tangible impact by positioning DoorDash as Canada's top platform.
 Own and execute the Canada expansion strategy : Build and execute a national roadmap focused on increasing our footprint while ensuring launch markets perform to expectations through rigorous marketplace management.
 Tactically run end-to-end execution : Lead the expansion lifecycle from initial strategy and buy-in through to execution, ensuring every launch is set up for long-term success.
 Right-size best practices : Apply proven operational frameworks while localizing strategies based on the specific marketplace dynamics of diverse Canadian cities.
 Lead cross-functional collaboration : Act as the connective tissue between the expansion team and DoorDash’s commercial units, surfacing insights and co-developing strategies that support national growth.
 Build strong internal relationships : Partner effectively with stakeholders across Dasher, Sales, Merchant, and Marketing teams to ensure a unified approach to marketplace health.
 Act like an Owner : Take full ownership of the success of our growth markets, with the autonomy to test, iterate, and scale what works across the country
 We’re excited about you because you have… 
 Are a builder and connector : You see opportunities where others see roadblocks. You’re energized by building systems from the ground up and forming lasting relationships along the way
 Have an operational mindset : You understand how to identify, scope, and execute high-impact initiatives, and you know how to align internal stakeholders to get things done.
 Thrive in ambiguity and autonomy : You’re comfortable setting your own direction, testing and learning as you go, and staying laser-focused on outcomes.
 Are operationally sharp and analytically driven : You turn insights into action and know how to measure and report on impact in a fast-moving environment.
 Qualifications 
 4+ years of experience in business development, consulting, strategy, startups, or operations
 Demonstrated experience working cross-functionally with commercial teams 
 Proven ability to identify growth opportunities and lead strategic initiatives from conception to execution
 Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence across various stakeholders and levels of the organization
 Proficient in Excel/Google Sheets and SQL; comfortable making decisions grounded in data
 Compensation 
 Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. 
 In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.
 $116,000 — $145,000 CAD

About the Role 
 As Program Specialist, Math – Elementary (K–6), you own the instructional design and quality of the courses in your subject. You decide how learning is designed and built, and whether the content meets the bar to go live. You report to the Director, Content & Curriculum – Elementary (K–6). 
 You work in a course team. The Product Manager owns the product vision, plan, scope and dates. You shape the instructional vision within that product vision. You lead the Content Producers who report to you, full-time and freelance: you coach them, set craft standards and review their work, while the Product Manager sets the team’s priorities. 
 This role suits an experienced educator with deep mathematics expertise and a strong grasp of how students develop in the subject. You are curious about how technology can improve the classroom. As the trusted voice of the classroom, you turn curriculum goals and classroom realities into engaging, effective and scalable learning in Edwin. 
 This posting represents an existing vacancy. 
 Key Accountabilities  
 Instructional design (30%) 
 Shape the instructional vision, learning outcomes and instructional approaches within the Product Manager’s product vision, during discovery and development. Contribute the instructional requirements to the Product Requirements Document (PRD). 
 Analyze new curriculum for what is new or different, and complete curriculum correlations. 
 Own the scope and sequence and learning pathways in Course Builder. Validate them with the Product Manager against the plan, and with Classroom Success and the Content Producers. 
 Own the subject instructional design style guide within our standard content development workflow, keeping it aligned with the curriculum, sound pedagogy, subject integrity, and real classroom use. 
 Design formative and summative assessment into every course from the start, to the K–12 assessment standards set by the Assessment Lead. Content Producers build the items. 
 Lead the thoughtful use of digital tools and emerging technologies in learning design. 
 Content quality (25%) 
 Serve as the subject-matter expert and educational advisor across the elementary mathematics portfolio. 
 Build and validate the first content prototype with Content Producers for early review. 
 Own the authoring instructions Content Producers use to create content, making sure they reflect the instructional design 
 Own quality throughout the build: accuracy, instructional integrity, CRRP alignment and classroom usability. Arbitrate review decisions; if the Product Manager disagrees, the Director breaks the tie. 
 Make sure all specialty content, such as First Nations, Métis and Inuit content, is created and reviewed by appropriate Indigenous voices. 
 Give quality sign-off before the Product Manager’s go-live decision. 
 Advise the Product Manager on accessibility, so the instructional design supports AODA (WCAG 2.2 AA). 
 Team leadership (25%) 
 Hire, supervise, coach and develop the Content Producers who report to you, and own their performance reviews, with formal input from the Product Managers they work with. 
 Onboard, train and direct Content Producers (full-time and freelance), authors and reviewers in pedagogy, the instructional design and classroom best practice. Give contributors clear feedback, and liaise with Content Services. 
 Define contributor skill sets, special skills (such as Indigenous perspectives and safety) and staffing needs with the Product Manager. 
 Voice of the classroom (10%) 
 Engage teachers, students and education stakeholders through classroom observations, user research, conferences and educator conversations, feeding the Product Manager’s discovery. Follow board research approval processes and Nelson’s privacy policies. 
 Build launch supports with the Product Manager, and train Commercial colleagues and customers after launch. 
 Support the Product Manager’s RFP and procurement responses, presentations and go-to-market initiatives. 
 Continuous improvement (10%) 
 Use performance data, educator feedback and student impact to optimize, update, reuse and scale high-performing content. 
 Carry out refreshes of existing content with Content Producers, including retrofitting assessment into existing courses, on the Product Manager’s plan. 
 Bring subject-specific feature requests to the Product Manager, and keep the Product Manager and Director updated on quality issues. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Make sure the scope and sequence, style guide, and content creation guidelines are ready by the dates set in the course plan. 
 Content passes review with few defects, and few quality issues are found after launch. 
 Teacher feedback rates the instructional quality of your courses highly. 
 Content Producers grow in capability, and are engaged and retained. 
 Requirements 
 University degree; certified educator (OCT or equivalent) preferred 
 7+ years of K–12 classroom or education experience, ideally in mathematics 
 5+ years of content development and lesson creation in K–12, EdTech or digital learning 
 Deep mathematics expertise, including student developmental trajectories, curriculum and assessment, across Ontario, Alberta and other provincial curricula 
 Strong instructional design and assessment design skills, translating curriculum into engaging learning experiences 
 People management experience (Content Producers report to this role) 
 Comfortable working in content authoring tools and digital content workflows; HTML an asset 
 Familiarity with emerging educational technologies and their classroom applications 
 Strong communication, collaboration and mentoring skills 
 Highly organized, adaptable and comfortable in a fast-paced environment 
 Strong commitment to improving student outcomes and educator experiences 
 Quick to master new tools for building content and working; judges all content critically against curriculum and pedagogy 
 French an asset 
 Who You Are 
 You bring 7+ years as a teacher, instructional coach or curriculum consultant, with deep subject expertise and a clear sense of how students develop across grades. 
 You design assessment as well as instruction, and you have led or coached other educators. 
 “If the design is right at the start, everything downstream gets easier.” 
 You coach producers rather than rewriting their work, and you enjoy watching them grow in skill. 
 You design with classroom data and Product Manager input, not alone. 
 You judge every draft critically against curriculum and pedagogy before it moves forward. 
 Creative problem solver: you find new ways to solve real teaching and learning problems, within out internal authoring tool, time and budget 
 UDL and differentiation: you meet every learner where they are, with entry points, supports and extensions 
 Modern and adaptable: you master new tools and techniques for building content and working quickly, and look for better ways of working, with expert judgment always leading 
 Compensation  
 The base salary for this permanent full-time position starts at $90,000 per annum based on experience. Compensation is part of our broader Total Rewards package, which includes benefits and programs that support employee well-being and growth. 
 Benefits   
 What We Offer  
 Health & Wellness 
 Financial & Professional Wellbeing 
 Pension plan (DCPP) with company matching contributions  
 Annual educational reimbursement for professional development 
 Flexibility & Time Off 
 Flexible work hours (divisional dependent) 
 Summer Fridays

Chez Tecsys, le logiciel que nous livrons permet aux hôpitaux, pharmacies et distributeurs d'avoir ce dont ils ont besoin, quand ils en ont besoin. Chaque rôle ici contribue à ce résultat.
 Pourquoi ce rôle est important 
 En tant que ingénieur fiabilité des infrastructures, vous vous joindrez à notre Centre des opérations réseau et de sécurité (NOC), une équipe au cœur de la fiabilité des plateformes pour les environnements SaaS critiques. Vous aiderez à maintenir, optimiser et assurer la fiabilité et la performance des systèmes qui alimentent notre infrastructure infonuagique sur AWS et Kubernetes, avec un fort accent sur l’automatisation, l’observabilité et l’amélioration continue.
 Ce poste combine l’ingénierie de la fiabilité avec la gestion des incidents, vous donnant une véritable responsabilité sur la disponibilité, la performance et l’innovation. Vous ferez partie d’une équipe hautement qualifiée qui valorise la résolution créative de problèmes, l’excellence opérationnelle et l’amélioration continue grâce à l’automatisation et à l’ingénierie de la résilience.
 Ce à quoi vous participerez 
 Tecsys est reconnue par des organisations essentielles des secteurs de la santé et de la distribution pour soutenir des chaînes d'approvisionnement résilientes, efficaces et sécurisées. Nous sommes un fournisseur mondial de logiciels infonuagiques propulsés par l'Intelligence artificielle (IA), coté à la Bourse de Toronto (TSX: TCS).
 Trois valeurs guident notre façon de travailler . Nous gagnons la confiance au quotidien en valorisant le client et en agissant avec intégrité. Nous nous entraidons en reconnaissant les forces individuelles et en travaillant en équipe. Et nous explorons avec audace en restant curieux et en nous adaptant pour réussir.
 Vous vous joindrez à une culture axée sur la curiosité, l'apprentissage continu et des gens qui repoussent les limites du possible.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Collaborer avec d’autres équipes d’ingénierie pour soutenir les services avant leur mise en service à travers des activités telles que la consultation en conception de systèmes, le développement de plateformes et de cadres logiciels, la planification des capacités et les revues de lancement. 
 Innover continuellement en identifiant les points faibles, en proposant des solutions créatives et en menant des initiatives qui simplifient, font évoluer et renforcent la plateforme. 
 Maintenir les services une fois qu’ils sont en ligne en mesurant et en surveillant la disponibilité, la latence et l’état général du système. 
 Assurer une observabilité optimisée : améliorer et élargir la surveillance et l’alerte à l’aide de Datadog; définir les SLO/SLI et créer des tableaux de bord exploitables qui génèrent des résultats de fiabilité. 
 Développer et favoriser l’automatisation : améliorer les outils internes, les cadres IaC et les pipelines (Terraform, GitLab CI/CD) afin de réduire les interventions manuelles et permettre des systèmes d’auto-réparation. 
 Faire évoluer les systèmes de façon durable par l’automatisation et en favorisant des changements qui améliorent la fiabilité et la rapidité. 
 Mettre en pratique une gestion durable des incidents et des analyses post-incident sans reproche. Diriger les examens post-incident (RCA) et identifier les correctifs à long terme qui améliorent la stabilité, la fiabilité et l’expérience des développeurs. 
 Mettre en œuvre la surveillance, la journalisation, l’alerte et le signalement des SLA. 
 Créer et maintenir une documentation technique. 
 Mettre en œuvre, maintenir et faire évoluer les meilleures pratiques SRE. 
 Agir comme commandant d’incident lors des incidents; coordonner la réponse interéquipes, gérer les communications et assurer une restauration rapide des services. 
 Autres exigences : 
 Rotation en cas d’escalade d’incidents
 Voyages occasionnels (visites trimestrielles sur les lieux, conférences - moins de 10 %)
 Ce que vous apportez 
 Solide expérience pertinente en ingénierie de la fiabilité des sites (SRE), en infonuagique ou en DevOps dans des environnements SaaS ou de production à grande échelle
 Solide expérience avec AWS (multicomptes, VPC, EC2, EKS) et Kubernetes à grande échelle
 Expertise pratique de l'infrastructure en tant que code et des outils d'automatisation (Terraform, Ansible ou équivalent)
 Expérience des pipelines CI/CD et de l'automatisation des mises en production (GitLab de préférence, Jenkins acceptable)
 Maîtrise des outils de surveillance et d'observabilité (Datadog ou équivalent), y compris les métriques, la journalisation, les alertes et les tableaux de bord
 Expérience de la conception, du déploiement et de l'exploitation de systèmes distribués à grande échelle et de plateformes multifournisseurs

 Connaissances de base des environnements de développement Java ou .NET
 Attitude proactive, avec un sens marqué de la responsabilisation, de la résolution de problèmes et du partage des connaissances
 Disposition à participer aux rotations de garde et à se déplacer occasionnellement au bureau (moins de 10 %)

Who we are
 About Stripe
 Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
 Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
 About the team
 Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data analysts and data scientists learn and grow together. You'll work with some of the most fundamental data at Stripe, and use that data to help drive company-wide initiatives. We have a variety of Data Analytics roles and teams across Stripe and will seek to align you to the most relevant team based on your background.
 What you’ll do
 As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business.  Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.

 Analyze data and running experiments to drive impact
 Ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly

 Extend Stripe’s metrics semantic layer
 Build new data assets and improve existing data assets to support decision-making, products, and business processes
 Assess the impact of decisions, product launches, and product improvements using business analytics and A/B testing
 Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
 Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns
 Who you are
 Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.

CE QUI NOUS REND EPIC ?
 INFOSEC
 Ce que nous faisons 
 Protéger les réseaux, le matériel et les personnes contre les risques pour la sécurité chez Epic. Mettre en place des outils de sécurité et des logiciels pour sécuriser l'infrastructure de systèmes et de données, tels que des pare-feu et des logiciels de cryptage. Établir les détails de tous les incidents, évaluer et signaler leurs impacts dès que possible.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 L’équipe des opérations de cyberdéfense d’Epic protège l’une des plus grandes communautés de joueurs au monde, ainsi que les employés, l’infrastructure et les technologies qui la soutiennent. En tant que directeur des opérations de cyberdéfense, vous assumerez l’entière responsabilité des activités de détection et d’intervention d’Epic, en dirigeant les équipes chargées de repérer, d’analyser et de contrer les menaces à l’échelle de l’entreprise. Vous définirez la vision à long terme des opérations de sécurité, bâtirez une organisation capable de suivre la croissance d’Epic et piloterez la transition vers des opérations automatisées et assistées par l’IA afin que l’équipe puisse se concentrer sur les menaces les plus critiques. Il s’agit d’un rôle de gestionnaire de proximité : vous montrerez l’exemple, resterez impliqué sur le terrain aux côtés de votre équipe et vous imposerez les mêmes standards d’excellence qu’aux autres.
 Ce dont vous serez responsable 
 Bâtir et diriger l’organisation des opérations de cyberdéfense en tant que gestionnaire impliqué sur le terrain : recruter et former des analystes aguerris, définir la structure organisationnelle et participer activement aux enquêtes, à la détection et aux incidents majeurs, tout en accompagnant l’équipe sur des cas concrets, en priorisant son perfectionnement et en éliminant les obstacles qui freinent son travail
 Établir la stratégie pluriannuelle et la feuille de route pour la détection, l’intervention, l’automatisation et les outils, en phase avec le profil de risque d’Epic, les priorités d’affaires et les objectifs de la direction de la sécurité de l’information 
 Agir à titre de responsable principal lors des incidents de sécurité les plus critiques d’Epic, en coordonnant les interventions avec les équipes de programmation, des affaires juridiques, de la protection de la vie privée, des communications et de la haute direction, et en présentant les impacts et les risques aux dirigeants 
 Assurer la couverture de détection et d’intervention dans les environnements infonuagiques, d’entreprise, de postes de travail, d’identité et de production, en orientant les investissements vers les menaces qui présentent le plus grand risque pour Epic 
 Promouvoir l’automatisation et les processus basés sur des agents d’IA au sein des opérations de sécurité, en collaborant avec les responsables de la programmation en sécurité pour établir des balises, des normes de validation et les étapes nécessitant une supervision humaine 
 Gérer les opérations de cyberdéfense comme un centre d’expertise et un partenaire stratégique pour le reste d’Epic : élaborer le budget et le portefeuille de fournisseurs (partenaires de services gérés, ententes de niveau de service, contrats et décisions de développement interne, d’achat ou de retrait d’outils), définir et suivre les indicateurs mesurant l’efficacité de notre protection (délai de détection, temps d’intervention, couverture, pertinence des alertes), maintenir les guides d’intervention, les rotations de garde et les mécanismes d’escalade à jour et prêts à évoluer, et tisser des liens à travers Epic pour transformer les menaces émergentes en actions concertées 
 Ce que nous recherchons 
 Plus de 8 ans d’expérience en opérations de sécurité, en réponse aux incidents ou en détection des menaces, dont plus de 6 ans à la tête d’équipes de sécurité 
 Expérience démontrée dans la mise sur pied et la mise à l’échelle d’un centre des opérations de sécurité (SOC) ou d’une organisation de détection et d’intervention, incluant la structure d’équipe, le recrutement et le mentorat de gestionnaires 
 Solide bagage technique sur les plateformes SIEM et EDR (p. ex. Splunk, Google SecOps, CrowdStrike, etc.), suffisant pour orienter les choix de conception et d’outils et remettre en question les approches techniques 
 Connaissance approfondie des méthodes des attaquants et des cadres de référence comme MITRE ATT&CK, ainsi que de leur application pour prioriser la couverture et les investissements 
 Expérience de la gestion d’incidents majeurs dans des environnements infonuagiques (AWS et/ou GCP), SaaS et des plateformes de gestion des identités, incluant les communications avec la haute direction et les organismes de réglementation 
 Expérience du déploiement de programmes d’automatisation et de SOAR à grande échelle, accompagnée d’une vision claire sur l’intégration responsable de l’IA aux opérations de sécurité 
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de budgets et la gestion de fournisseurs et de prestataires de services de sécurité gérés, incluant les contrats, les ententes de niveau de service et le suivi de la performance 
 Un leader calme, imputable et axé sur l’humain : capable de trancher sous pression, de vulgariser clairement les risques et les compromis auprès des dirigeants dans des breffages et rapports d’incident, de mettre la main à la pâte avec son équipe sur les enquêtes, la détection et les incidents, et de remettre en question les façons de faire établies. Vous assumez les résultats, assurez un suivi rigoureux, prenez vos responsabilités lorsque les choses tournent mal et mesurez votre réussite à celle de votre équipe et des personnes qu’elle protège

 RESPONSIBILITIES

À propos de Mila 
 Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions au domaine de l’apprentissage profond, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
 Sommaire du poste
 Le Lab d'IA souveraine est une nouvelle initiative de Mila visant à assembler une pile (un stack)  d'inférence IA open source prête pour l'entreprise, que les organisations peuvent déployer et exploiter sur des infrastructures sous leur contrôle. Elle combine le service de modèles, la recherche d'information (RAG), l'orchestration d'agents et l'observabilité, avec un plan de contrôle pour les gérer comme un produit unique.
 Sous la responsabilité du directeur principal de l'ingénierie logicielle, vous concevrez et maintiendrez les paquets de déploiement et l'automatisation de la pile d'IA. Ceux-ci permettront aux partenaires de déployer, mettre à jour et restaurer la pile sur leur propre infrastructure, depuis un nœud unique jusqu'à des grappes Kubernetes en production. Vous travaillerez avec l'équipe d'intégration pour paqueter leurs composants et les déployer dans des environnements de référence à l'aide de flux de travail partagés. Vous recommandez des technologies de plateforme sur la base de tests reproductibles, d'exigences opérationnelles et de la pertinence de l'architecture. Ce rôle ne comprend pas de support de production ni de garde (on-call).

 The Role 
 You're taking over an existing book of established client relationships. These are not new clients figuring out what they bought. They've been with us, they know the product, and they have expectations built on months of experience with the business.
 Your job is to keep them progressing, keep them retained, and keep them expanding. That means understanding where each client actually is in their business, what's working, what's stuck, and what they need next. Not checking in for the sake of it. Actually moving the needle on their results.
 This is a consulting role disguised as account management. You're not managing a spreadsheet of renewals. You're advising business owners on how to grow: how to frame their offer, how to think about their funnel, how to close deals, how to handle fulfillment, and how to use AI to do all of it faster.

 An established portfolio of legacy clients across various stages of maturity and engagement
 Regular check-ins, growth workshops, and strategic conversations with business owners who are building and scaling real companies

 Business consulting — advising clients on offer framing, lead generation strategy, sales process, prospecting, closing, and fulfillment. You need to understand these well enough to coach, not just relay information
 Upsell identification — knowing when a client is ready for more and positioning the next step as the natural move, not a sales pitch
 Cross-functional coordination with the onboarding, deliverables, and office hours teams to make sure nothing falls through the cracks
 Documentation — every interaction, decision, and next step logged so anyone picking up your account knows exactly where things stand

Position Summary  
 The People AI Solutions Designer is the builder. Where the People AI Deployment Lead readies HR processes for automation, the Solutions Designer takes that readied work and builds it — rapidly prototyping, coding, and shipping the agents, automations, and lightweight apps that solve real HR problems.   
 This is a hands-on craft role for someone who moves quickly from problem to working prototype to production. The Designer “vibe-builds” and assembles solutions in low-code and agent platforms and dropping into code where it is faster or better — and partners closely with the Deployment Lead, HR Systems, and McKesson Technology to put durable solutions into the hands of HR. Select solutions may be managed from idea to launch from within HR with limited oversight, and more complex solutions may require a handoff to MT to fully implement.   
 Key Responsibilities  
 Translate Readied Workflows into Technical Designs  (20%)  
 Take defined inputs, outputs, decision points, and ownership and turn them into a concrete solution design or mockup.  
 Make pragmatic build decisions — what an agent handles, what is automated, what stays human — and flag where a process needs more readiness before it can be built.  
 Build & Prototype Solutions  (30%)  
 Build agents, automations, and lightweight apps that solve the HR problems surfaced and readied by process owners across HR & partners within the Workforce Innovation team  
 Rapidly prototype — turn a readied workflow into a working build quickly, favoring momentum and learning over perfection, then refine based on user feedback  
 Build across low-code and agent platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot Studio / Power Platform, ServiceNow, Moveworks) and drop into code (Python, scripting, APIs) where it is the better tool.  
 Lead the prototype and build, partnering closely with UX designer for interface designs and McKesson Technology for complex enterprise solutions  
 Iterate from Real Usage  (20%)  
 Pilot solutions with real users, instrument them, and improve based on actual usage and performance.  
 Tune prompts, logic, and integrations to raise quality, reliability, and experience.  
 Harden, Document & Hand to Operations  (15%)  
 Harden solutions for production including error handling, guardrails, data handling, and monitoring and document how they work. Fully ready the solution for transition and lifecycle management.  
 Hand solutions to HR Systems / operations / COE owners for ongoing ownership, in line with the standards set by the Deployment Lead.  
 Maintain a Reusable Build Toolkit & Standards  (15%)  
 Build and curate reusable components, patterns, and templates so each new solution ships faster than the last.  
 Contribute to shared build, security, and quality standards for AI and automation in HR.  
 What Success Looks Like  
 Readied HR workflows are turned into working, deployed solutions on a short cycle.  
 Solutions are reliable in production, well-documented, and cleanly handed to operations.  
 A growing library of reusable components shortens the build time for each new solution.  
 Measurable capacity, cycle-time, and experience gains are realized from shipped builds.  
 Demonstrates a repeatable “ready-then-build” model that scales across HR.  
 Minimum Job Qualifications  
 Education / Training  
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in computer science, information systems, design, engineering, or a related field — or equivalent demonstrated building experience.  
 Certifications in relevant low-code / agent platforms (e.g., Power Platform, Copilot Studio, ServiceNow) preferred.  
 Business Experience  
 Typically 7+ years of relevant experience building automations, agents, integrations, or applications, consistent with a P5 individual contributor.  
 Demonstrated portfolio of solutions taken from prototype to production. HR or enterprise-process context is a plus.  
 Specialized Knowledge & Skills  
 Fluency with low-code / agent platforms and the ability to drop into code (Python, scripting, APIs) when it is faster or better.  
 Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agent tooling; prompt, logic, and integration design.  
 Comfort with ambiguity; moves from problem to working prototype quickly and iterates from real usage.  
 Builds for reliability, quality, security, and maintainability, and documents and hands off cleanly.  
 Collaboration mindset, working in tight partnership with the HR COE or Process owner, Process Readiness lead, HR Systems, and McKesson Technology.  
 Why This Role Matters  
 This role brings a new skillset (citizen development) out of enterprise technology and in to HR to sit alongside process owners and automate the daily tasks that take administrative lift. Allows for greater strategic capacity, and ensures repeated reliable process handoffs across complex HR teams.  
 The People AI Duo  
 This role is one half of a deliberate two-person operating model for AI and automation in HR. The People AI Deployment Lead goes out across HR to find the work that is ripe for automation and gets it ready for automation. This role, the People AI Solutions Designer, takes that readied work and builds a rapid prototype, and codes, and ships the agents and automations to manage the process. Together the duo can be deployed against any HR process, end to end: one readies, one builds, and a repeatable model for scaling AI across HR takes hold.

$122,100 - $162,800

 Our engineering organization is what makes that trust possible, from the AI pipeline and models that extract the data, to the labeling tools, to the customer-facing product our clients use every day.
 Transforming this industry takes the right people. If you want to build the engineering behind AI, expert human review, and customer trust, we’d love to meet you.
 About you and the role 
 You build the systems that power our AI pipeline. Every document our clients upload passes through services you design and maintain, and the reliability and speed of those services determine how quickly our customers can move claims forward.
 You are a thoughtful back end engineer who writes efficient, reusable, and reliable Python, understands data structures and algorithms, and enjoys solving performance and scalability problems. You document your architectural decisions clearly and work well with front end and ML engineers.
 Our platform connects computer vision and generative models to the work of making sense of intricate legal and medical documents. Wisedocs spent the past year rebuilding its core technical platform from the ground up, including our back end, and that foundation is now in place. Our largest customers have doubled with us in the past year, and they are counting on the platform to stay fast and dependable as it grows.
 You will work across our Data Delivery and Core Platform teams, with close partnership from Machine Learning, to build and scale the services that move documents and data through our pipeline, from upload to download.

 ·      Build and scale the services that move documents and data through our pipeline, from upload to download
 ·      Identify and resolve performance and scalability issues to improve the robustness of the system
 ·      Design data models and handle complex data structures and algorithms to keep processing accurate and fast
 ·      Integrate models and processes from our Machine Learning team into the processing pipeline
 ·      Work with front end engineers to design APIs and connect user-facing features to server-side logic
 ·      Create and maintain technical documentation for system components and architecture, including the reasoning behind key decisions
 ·      Contribute to automation across the Agile development, build, and deployment lifecycle

 ·      Experience with a cloud platform such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure

 ·      A robust problem-solving mindset, comfortable navigating frequently changing work items and scope, and able to manage multiple tasks efficiently

Distributors operate on thin margins, maintain tight service levels, and navigate complex networks of suppliers, warehouses, carriers, and sales channels. They are looking for an ERP that does more than record transactions. They want one that helps them anticipate demand, move inventory faster, and fulfill orders accurately. 
 Acumatica is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the product direction for our Distribution Edition. You will translate what wholesale and distribution customers need into a clear roadmap, work side by side with engineering and our partner ecosystem to deliver it and make Acumatica the obvious choice for growing distributors. 
 Distribution Capabilities You Will Own 
 Inventory and warehouse management, order management and fulfillment, purchasing and procurement, pricing and rebates, and demand planning and replenishment. 
 What You'll Do 
 Own the Distribution Roadmap 
 Define and communicate a multi-year product vision and roadmap for Distribution, aligned to corporate strategy and our other industry editions. 
 Turn customer, partner, and market insight into prioritized market requirements that engineering can build against. 
 Build the business case for planned investments so leadership can make informed decisions on scope, timing, and tradeoffs. 
 Make deliberate build, buy, and partner choices, including where our ISV ecosystem should lead. 
 Bring AI into Distribution Workflows 
 Identify where AI should automate, assist, or keep a human in the loop across demand forecasting, replenishment, order exceptions, pricing, and warehouse operations. 
 Design for the trust, transparency, and control that operations teams require. 
 Define measurable outcomes such as inventory turns, fill rate, order accuracy, and time saved, and hold the roadmap accountable to them. 
 Know the Market and the Customer 
 Spend time with distributors, resellers, and ISV partners to understand how they run their operations and where Acumatica wins or loses.
 Track competitors and market trends and turn them into clear differentiation for sales and marketing. 
 Serve as the subject matter expert for Distribution inside and outside the company. 
 Deliver and Launch 
 Partner with engineering and UX on design, scope, and delivery, and review functional designs and release plans.
 Lead launch readiness across the organization: beta programs, early adopters, documentation and training review, and enablement for sales, support, and services.
 Create the collateral that makes new capabilities easy to sell, including demos, data sheets, and presentations.
 Monitor product quality and adoption metrics and drive improvements. 
 Support Customer and Partner Success 
 Resolve escalations from support, customer success, and implementation teams. 
 Contribute to knowledge base content and partner education. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 A Distribution roadmap that customers, partners, and internal teams rally behind. 
 Capabilities in the market that customers adopt and can measure.
 Stronger win rates, expansion, and retention in Distribution accounts.
 A healthy partner ecosystem extending the edition where it matters most.
Experience 
 7+ years of product management experience in business applications, in the ERP space.
 Direct domain experience in the distribution vertical market and product experience with inventory, warehouse management, order management, purchasing, and supply chain management.
 Track record of taking products from market requirements through launch with measurable results.
 Experience working with ISVs, partners, or other platform ecosystems.

 Strong roadmap and prioritization skills, with decisions tied to customer value and business outcomes.
